Experimental centerline pseudomeasurements; σ is assumed measurement uncertainty, not achieved accuracy. The previous causal automatic association schedule is fixed across sigma runs. No new road association or GNSS-bias model is introduced. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0). No map API, external scripts, fonts, or network requests. Repository default navigation is unchanged.

One persistent estimator—not a switched output

The blue baseline and the green map-aided EKF each start from a new native runtime and receive every original IMU and GNSS event in the same causal order. The green state is never replaced by the blue state. Before its first map update it is bit-identical to blue.

At a valid map epoch a scalar centerline pseudomeasurement uses residual d and variance R = σ². The full-state Kalman update uses S = HPHᵀ + R, K = PHᵀ/S, Δx = −Kd, and Joseph-form posterior covariance. The native runtime applies its normal error-state injection/reset. Normal covariance propagation and GNSS updates continue afterward.

Association gates the next measurement, not the output. An ambiguous road, missing geometry, finite-edge failure, incompatible heading, or rejected error-state increment skips that measurement without changing the state or covariance. A native numerical failure aborts replay instead of silently switching outputs. Previously consumed 10 m map cells remain consumed across gaps.

Controlled experiment: the original automatic road-association schedule is frozen, not recomputed from the corrected estimate. All seven sigma settings use the same schedule. This tests persistent correction, not a newly qualified closed-loop road-association system. No surveyed reference or expected itinerary is supplied to the filter.

Interpretation: strong centerline constraints may pull the estimate away from the vehicle's actual lane. Persistent corrections can also persist when an earlier road choice was wrong; dedicated integrity recovery is not implemented here. Continuous means persistent recursive state—not a guarantee of a smooth curve or constant accuracy.

Four complete recordings × seven sigma settings were freshly replayed through the existing pinned 18-state Rust runtime. Every sensor is processed at its recorded timestamp; this compact viewer exports the original approximately 1 Hz epochs. Slider changes select precomputed numerical replays and preserve the current time and camera. The browser does not rerun the filter.
